title: Lab 3C — Route 53 advanced routing
topic: Route 53 routing policies (simple, weighted, latency, failover, geolocation), health checks, alias vs CNAME, DNS-layer DR vs ALB health, witcoskitech.com lab subdomains, GSA multi-Region failover awareness
format: 15 timed scenario questions (~24 min, ~96 sec each). Reinforces night-25-route53-routing.md and night-25-lab-route53-setup scripts. Answer without peeking at night-25-quiz-answers.json first.
answerDistribution: A×4 B×4 C×4 D×3 — options shuffled so correct letter varies

questions.question: witcoskitech.com uses a single A alias to CloudFront with no routing policy. A stakeholder asks for 10% of DNS answers to hit a canary CloudFront distribution before full cutover. Which Route 53 policy fits?

options.A: Weighted routing — two records with SetId values and weights 90 and 10
options.B: Failover routing — PRIMARY and SECONDARY without a health check
options.C: Simple routing — add a second A record with the same name
options.D: Geolocation routing — route 10% of countries to the canary

questions.question: GSA prod designs DR: primary ALB in us-east-1 serves api.globalskiatlas.com; secondary is an S3 static maintenance site in us-west-2. Route 53 must stop sending users to the primary when the app is down. Minimum DNS configuration?

options.A: Latency records in both Regions — failover is automatic
options.B: Weighted 50/50 between ALB and S3 — health inferred from HTTP 503
options.C: Failover PRIMARY alias to ALB with a Route 53 health check; SECONDARY to S3 — no check on secondary
options.D: Multivalue answer returning both ALB and S3 A records simultaneously

questions.question: You deploy identical API stacks in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Users worldwide should hit the lowest-latency Region. Which Route 53 policy?

options.A: Weighted routing with equal weights — latency is automatic
options.C: Latency routing — one latency record per Region pointing at each regional endpoint
options.D: Simple routing — Route 53 measures all AWS Regions and picks the fastest

questions.question: night-25-lab creates night25-failover.witcoskitech.com. PRIMARY aliases CloudFront with an HTTPS health check; SECONDARY aliases www. The health check shows Unhealthy for 5 minutes but clients still resolve PRIMARY. Likely cause?

options.A: SECONDARY record also needs the same health check ID attached
options.B: Failover requires NLB — CloudFront aliases cannot use health checks
options.C: Clients or recursive resolvers cache the prior DNS answer until TTL expires
options.D: Health checks only work with private hosted zones associated to a VPC

questions.question: EU privacy rules require EU visitors to resolve to an eu-west-1 CloudFront distribution; everyone else uses us-east-1. Which policy?

options.A: Latency routing — EU is always lowest latency for EU users
options.B: Weighted routing — set EU weight to 100 and US weight to 0
options.C: Failover routing — EU is PRIMARY, US is SECONDARY
options.D: Geolocation routing — Continent or Country records for EU plus a default record

questions.question: Exam scenario: apex domain example.com must point at a CloudFront distribution. Why is an A/AAAA alias preferred over a CNAME at the zone apex?

options.A: CNAME records are not permitted at the zone apex per DNS rules
options.B: CloudFront only accepts CNAME targets, not alias records
options.C: Alias records require a longer TTL than CNAME — better for apex
options.D: CNAME at apex is allowed but costs more per query than alias

questions.question: An ALB in us-east-1 spans three AZs. One AZ loses power; targets in other AZs stay healthy. Clients use the ALB DNS name directly (no Route 53 routing policy). What happens?

options.A: All traffic fails until Route 53 failover flips to secondary
options.B: New connections reach healthy ALB nodes in remaining AZs — ALB is multi-AZ
options.C: Route 53 automatically creates weighted records per AZ
options.D: Clients must switch to the NLB DNS name manually

questions.question: night-25-lab aliases lab subdomains to CloudFront using hosted zone ID Z2FDTNDATAQYW2. What does that constant represent?

options.A: The us-east-1 regional hosted zone for all S3 buckets
options.B: Your account-specific CloudFront distribution ID encoded as a zone
options.C: The global Route 53 hosted zone ID used for CloudFront alias targets
options.D: The private hosted zone ID for VPC endpoint DNS names

questions.question: Route 53 health check on https://witcoskitech.com/HTML/index.html reports Healthy while the ALB behind a separate api.example.com returns 502. Why can both be true?

options.A: One health check monitors the static site; ALB target health is separate
options.B: Route 53 health checks always mirror ALB target group state
options.C: HTTPS health checks cannot run against CloudFront distributions
options.D: Health checks only apply to failover SECONDARY records

questions.question: You want Route 53 to return up to eight healthy A record IPs so clients pick one at random. No Application Load Balancer in the design. Which policy?

options.A: Weighted routing with eight equal weights on the same name
options.B: Multivalue answer routing with health checks on each record
options.C: Latency routing with eight Regions in one account
options.D: Geoproximity routing with bias zero in every Region

questions.question: You run night-25-lab-route53-teardown.ps1 after practice. What remains in AWS?

options.A: Entire witcoskitech.com hosted zone deleted — domain unregister required
options.B: Apex witcoskitech.com and www records plus CloudFront — night25-* records and lab health check removed
options.C: All Route 53 records deleted including production apex aliases
options.D: CloudFront distribution deleted — S3 bucket becomes public website only

questions.question: GSA compares Route 53 latency routing vs AWS Global Accelerator for worldwide API traffic. Best differentiator for the exam?

options.A: Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs and TCP/UDP edge steering; Route 53 latency is DNS-level Region selection
options.B: Route 53 latency routing works only with CloudFront; Global Accelerator only with ALB
options.C: Global Accelerator cannot health-check endpoints; Route 53 always can
options.D: Latency routing requires health checks; Global Accelerator does not use health at all

questions.question: Hybrid exam: on-prem servers must resolve internal-only hostnames like db.corp.local inside the VPC while public users resolve globalskiatlas.com on the internet. Which Route 53 feature for internal names?

options.A: Public hosted zone with geolocation routing
options.B: Private hosted zone associated with the VPC
options.C: Latency routing on the apex domain
options.D: CloudFront alternate domain name for db.corp.local

questions.question: Failover PRIMARY points to an ALB alias. Operators want Route 53 to fail over when any single unhealthy target remains behind the ALB. What is the exam-accurate approach?

options.A: Enable Route 53 child health checks that evaluate ALB target health, or monitor a composite condition
options.B: Set ALB health check interval to 1 second — Route 53 inherits automatically
options.C: Use weighted routing — unhealthy targets get weight 0 automatically
options.D: Attach the health check only to the SECONDARY record

questions.question: night-25-lab uses night25-simple.witcoskitech.com with simple routing (one alias). Production apex witcoskitech.com uses the same pattern. What changes when you add weighted records on a different subdomain?

options.A: Simple routing on apex is replaced by weighted at the zone level
options.B: Nothing on apex — routing policy is per record set name; lab subdomains are independent
options.C: CloudFront requires a new distribution per routing policy type
options.D: Health checks become mandatory for all records in the hosted zone
